Looking at the cuboid (4×2×2), I can track the visible cubes of each colour:

- **Dark grey:** the left end column plus one cube along the bottom front.
- **Light grey:** the top front row of three plus one cube below the middle.
- **Black:** the right end (bottom front, bottom back, top back).
- **White:** only two top faces show (middle of the back top row).

The remaining hidden cubes are the back‑bottom left two cubes. Giving these to the white piece makes it a flat "S/Z" shape: two cubes on the bottom row with two cubes on top shifted one step along — exactly the shape in option C. Checking the other options: D (2×2 slab) would force the black piece to be disconnected; A, B, E would require white cubes in positions already showing other colours.

\boxed{C}
